title: Karnataka Restaurants Escalate Revolt Against Swiggy and Zomato With August 15 Ultimatum
excerpt: Hotel and restaurant associations across Karnataka, from Bengaluru to tier-2 cities like Belagavi, are threatening a mass delisting from food delivery platforms over unauthorized deductions and crushing commissions.
body:
• The Bengaluru Hotel and Restaurant Association (BHRA) has issued an August 15 deadline for Swiggy and Zomato to resolve grievances over unauthorized discounts, opaque payouts, and order cancellation losses, or face a city-wide delisting.
  • The revolt is spreading beyond Bengaluru to Karnataka's tier-2 cities, with hotel associations in places like Belagavi joining the statewide push for fairer food delivery practices.
  • Rapido's zero-commission food delivery platform Ownly, which signed an MoU with the National Restaurant Association of India (NRAI), claims nearly 10% of Bengaluru's online food delivery market since its March launch.
  • Commissions of 25-35% charged by Swiggy and Zomato have become unsustainable for restaurants where delivery now accounts for up to 50% of revenue, up from 10% before the pandemic.

A Deadline for Independence Day

Restaurants and hotel operators across Karnataka have drawn a line in their long-running dispute with food delivery platforms Swiggy and Zomato, threatening to pull thousands of eateries off the apps starting August 15 unless the companies address a list of financial grievances.

The ultimatum, led by the Bengaluru Hotel and Restaurant Association (BHRA), reflects years of escalating friction between traditional dining establishments and food tech aggregators. Restaurant owners argue that while operating costs like rent, staff wages, and raw materials continue to surge, arbitrary platform practices have severely eroded their margins.

BHRA President PC Rao said the current financial model has become unsustainable. Unless Swiggy and Zomato provide formal, written assurances to address systemic issues, thousands of popular Bengaluru eateries plan to turn off their aggregator terminals en masse.

Grievances Run Deep

The pushback centers on several long-standing financial complaints. Restaurant associations allege that platforms frequently auto-apply steep promotional discounts and levy advertising campaign charges without explicit, written consent from restaurant owners. Platform policies automatically deduct money from restaurant payouts immediately after a customer files a complaint, with no room for the establishment to verify the claim.

Restaurants are also forced to absorb the entire loss when orders are cancelled after food has already been prepared—a practice that owners say punishes them for problems beyond their control.

The BHRA's demands include an absolute freeze on unauthorized promotional deductions, transparent and itemized monthly settlement statements, dedicated relationship managers for dispute resolution, and fair policies on order cancellations and customer complaints.

Revolt Spreads Beyond Bengaluru

The movement is not limited to the state capital. Hotel and restaurant associations in tier-2 Karnataka cities, including Belagavi, have signaled their support for the statewide push. In Belagavi, where a growing number of restaurants rely on platform-driven delivery to reach customers, hoteliers have echoed the same complaints about opaque deductions and unsustainable commission structures that range from 25% to 35% of every order.

"Before Covid-19, food delivery was just 10% of a restaurant's business. Today, it is the heart of the business. When your heart of the business becomes 50%, we had never done the pricing where a 20% commission was factored in."

— Sagar Daryani, NRAI President and Wow! Momo co-founder

Rapido's Ownly Seizes the Opening

The growing discontent has created an opening for new entrants. Rapido's zero-commission food delivery platform Ownly, launched in Bengaluru in March after a pilot that began last year, claims to have captured nearly 10% of the city's online food delivery market. Earlier this week, Rapido integrated Ownly into its main app, making food ordering available alongside its existing bike taxi and auto services.

Ownly signed a memorandum of understanding with the NRAI, which represents over 50,000 restaurants nationwide. The platform charges no commissions or listing fees; instead, customers pay a separate delivery fee to cover logistics costs. Flipkart is also preparing to enter food delivery, starting in Bengaluru.

What's Next

NRAI President Daryani said he remains optimistic the issues can be resolved through dialogue. "I think the heat is being experienced by them and they understand where we are coming from," he said. But the August 15 deadline looms, and restaurant owners across Karnataka appear prepared to follow through.

For the Indian diaspora with family ties to Karnataka, the outcome could reshape how restaurants in their hometowns operate. If the revolt succeeds in lowering commission structures, it could improve margins for the small family-run eateries that remain cultural touchstones for NRIs visiting cities like Bengaluru, Belagavi, and Mysuru.
